evidence_statement: Hazards collected through interviews and site visits were organized, categorized, and prioritized for inclusion in the AR and VR models.

evidence_statement: The AR model exposed trainees to hazard types and their associated risks and consequences.

evidence_statement: The VR canvases guided trainees toward ways to mitigate or prevent the consequences of encountered hazards.

evidence_statement: The AR part of the implemented training was primarily concerned with theoretical and managerial aspects.

evidence_statement: Each AR hazard was hosted on a separate image on a physical paper identified as the hazard sheet.

case_title: Enhancing Bridges’ Safety Training Using Augmented Reality and Virtual Reality
evidence_statement: Safety managers with 14-to-20-plus years of experience were interviewed about hazards encountered in bridge construction.

evidence_statement: The authors concluded that increased knowledge acquisition increased trainees’ hazard awareness.

evidence_statement: Post-training results showed significant improvement in trainees’ ability to identify hazards missed before training.

case_title: Enhancing Bridges’ Safety Training Using Augmented Reality and Virtual Reality
evidence_statement: Trainees showed improved assessment of risk severity, likelihood, and potential impact during VR and after training.
